equation_summary: Two covariance states per token (naive.py:22-23,59-62): h_kk <- exp(g_t) h_kk + (beta_t k_t) ⊗ k_t and h_kv <- exp(g_t) h_kv + (beta_t k_t) ⊗ v_t, with per-head scalar log decay g. The read is a REGULARIZED PER-TOKEN SOLVE: x_t = argmin ||h_kk_t x - q_t||^2 + ||lamb .* x||^2 with per-head-channel regularizer lamb, approximated by ~30 conjugate-gradient iterations (naive.py:26-39, max_CG_iteration=30, eps 1e-5) initialized from q/(diag(h_kk)+lamb); then o_t = x_t^T h_kv_t. Layer: q/k L2-normed, beta=sigmoid, g=logsigmoid, lamb = softplus(lambda_params)+0.25 lower bound (layers/mesa_net.py:101-106,167-172). Both states updated BEFORE the solve, so the read is after-update but through a nonlinear solve, not a contraction.
ledger_verdicts: CONFIRM call graph E[Q/K normalization/regularizer] ; B[K2 two covariance states+regularized per-token solve] ; E[output]: the mixer genuinely carries two states and replaces the linear read with a regularized per-token CG solve (naive.py:26-40) — the blocked semantics are exactly as named.

CONFIRM 'Solver tolerance/iterations, implicit VJP and nonzero-state gradients': the solve is iterative (30 CG steps, 1e-5 epsilon floors at naive.py:33,37) with no exact-gradient guarantee, so an implicit-VJP descriptor and tolerance policy are required; both states accept nonzero init (naive.py:53-54).

CONFIRM read timing nuance for the ledger: both covariance states are updated with the current token BEFORE the solve (naive.py:59-64), i.e. the solve sees h_kk/h_kv including the current write — after-update read through a nonlinear operator.
direction_justification: The per-token regularized nonlinear inner solve (CG over the running covariance) is an architecture-specific read that cannot share the closed linear-delta law and would impose a solver tolerance/iteration contract no other mixer needs — keep as external comparator.
open_questions: Whether the CG iteration count (30), 1e-5 epsilon floors, and warm-start q/(diag(h_kk)+lamb) are part of the semantic descriptor or a numerical-policy field — they change the output.
Whether an implicit-function VJP through the fixed point is even well-defined at 30 truncated iterations, or whether unrolled-solve gradients are the only honest reference.
